environment: read-only probe of the live production health endpoint from the certification workstation

discrepancy.finding: The live deployment does not serve the SHA the release evidence records. EV-RELEASE-IDENTITY declares healthSha 9fa36d3bcac6532f0c6f07af9045825a9d97844f, deployed at 2026-08-22T06:38:07.408Z. The endpoint reports e968ce7b585fb6afaa64c8aae7ee24d1ba013dd6, built 2026-08-22T10:02:02Z — roughly three and a half hours later.
discrepancy.interpretation: Production was redeployed to e968ce7 after the release-identity evidence was written, and the evidence was never regenerated. certification.config.json already anticipated this: the note superseding 9fa36d3 says e968ce7 "is the merge commit CI built and published an image for, and is the commit to deploy". The deploy happened as planned; only the record was left behind.
discrepancy.whyItMatters: Nothing in the repository could have detected this. Every check that reads the deployed SHA reads it from EV-RELEASE-IDENTITY, so the stale value was self-consistent across the whole certification package. It took probing the live endpoint to see it. A release record that is never re-measured describes the deployment it was written for, not the one that is running.

NOT_VERIFIED: Web and worker image digests. The health endpoint reports the commit, not the running image digest; confirming the digests needs access to the deployment host, which this checkout does not have.
Whether the worker is on the same build as web. A mixed deployment would not be visible from this endpoint.
metrics.closesWhen: the candidate is deployed and /api/health reports the candidate SHA, with web and worker digests confirmed equal to the certified image digest
